Oblivion ESM/ESP binary format confirmed: 20-byte record header (NOT the 16-byte header used by Skyrim/Fallout). Record = tag(4) + dataSize(4) + flags(4) + formID(4) + version(2) + unknown(2) = 20 bytes. GRUP = 'GRUP'(4) + size(4) + label(4) + groupType(4) + skip(4) = 20 bytes. Subrecord = tag(4) + size(2) = 6 bytes, with size masked by (size & 0xFFFF). TES4 header record sits at offset 0 with dataSize=744, flags=1, formID=0, so the first GRUP is at offset 764 (20 + 744). app/src/main/cpp/assets/esm_reader.cpp already implements this format correctly (L116 'TES4 record: 20-byte header', L183 'remaining 16 bytes', L86 'GRUP header (20 bytes)', L471 size & 0xFFFF + offset += 6). CRITICAL: records with size 0 are LEGAL and are NOT terminators; treating them as errors truncates the scan.

Oblivion Script VM instruction format (confirmed from script_vm.cpp and script_disasm.cpp): each instruction is opcode(uint16 LE) + argLength(uint16 LE) + argData(argLength), i.e. a 4-byte header. argLength==0 instructions (ADD/POP/NEG/CMP) still consume 4 bytes. STOP must be 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00. Opcode values: STOP=0x0000, ADD=0x0001, NEG=0x0006, JUMP=0x0010, JUMP_Z=0x0011, PUSH_INT=0x0012, PUSH_FLOAT=0x0013, PUSH_REF=0x0015, POP=0x0016, DUP=0x0017, GET_LOCAL=0x0020, GET_GLOBAL=0x0022, CALL=0x1000. JUMP/JUMP_Z targets are ABSOLUTE program counters (ctx.setPC(target)), not relative offsets. execute(ctx, maxInstructions) returns VMResult::FrameBudget when the budget is exhausted.

app/src/main/cpp/include/glm/glm.hpp is a hand-written minimal GLM stub, NOT real GLM. vec3 exposes only vec3(), vec3(x,y,z), public x/y/z, operator+ - * /, dot, cross, length, normalize. There is NO operator[] and NO single-float constructor, so 'v[i]' and 'glm::vec3(0.0f)' fail to compile. Use explicit component math or copy into a float array, and always pass three floats to the constructor. Free functions glm::dot / glm::cross / glm::length / glm::normalize do exist.

QuestManager semantics (deliberate, do not 'fix'): updateObjectiveProgress() auto-completes a quest as soon as allObjectivesCompleted() is true, by calling checkAndCompleteQuest() -> completeQuest(). completeQuest() is NOT idempotent - it returns false and logs a warning if the quest is already COMPLETED (failQuest() is symmetric). Auto-completion is called from both updateObjectiveProgress() and update(). QuestStageManager::checkCompletionStage() forwards completeQuest()'s bool, but its only call site (quest_stage_manager.cpp:350) discards it, so the non-idempotent result causes no production harm.

CharacterStatus::initialize(baseHealth, baseMana, level) no longer applies level scaling; it sets maxHealth = baseHealth, maxMana = baseMana, and now also stores this->level = level. CollisionWorld::getBodyCount() now returns the new liveBodyCount_ member instead of bodies.size(). bodies is a slot array: addBody() reuses freeSlots or push_backs, and removeBody() only sets id=-1, isActive=false and push_backs the slot, so the vector never shrinks. removeBody() also gained a double-free guard (if bodies[bodyId].id == NULL_BODY return;). getBodyCount() has no production consumers - only Phase30 tests - so the capacity->live-count change is behaviour-neutral outside tests.

Consequently maxMagicka is NEVER persisted. Changing only L686 to maxMagicka would mix two attributes into one stat, so decide first whether Player gets a real magicka pool. Oblivion MGEF/SPEL/ENCH/INGR/ALCH binary layout (empirically confirmed with Python probes mgef_probe7..12 against the real Oblivion.esm). MGEF subrecord is DATA (36 or 64 bytes; NOT MEDT): off4=baseCost(float), off8=actorValue(uint32), off12=school(0-5), off16=flags. SPEL subrecord SPIT is 16 bytes: off0=spellType, off4=cost, off8=level, off12=uninitialized (0xCDCDCD00; NOT flags). EFID (4 bytes) is the MGEF editorID ASCII code (e.g. FIDG, RESP, INVI), NOT a formID. EFIT is 24 bytes: off0-3 = EFID echo, off4=magnitude, off8=area, off12=duration, off16=unused, off20=actorValue. The old code read magnitude/area/duration from off0/off4/off8, i.e. 4 bytes off; that was the direct cause of 0 spells being assigned. INGR/ALCH: DATA is only 4 bytes (float weight) and ENIT is 8 bytes (off0=value, off4=flags).

Oblivion EFIT magnitude is stored as EITHER int32 OR float depending on the record (proven by mgef_probe11: int values appear as denormal floats such as 1.4e-45). Read it with the helper readFloatOrInt() in assets/esm_reader.cpp: if the float is 0, non-finite, |f|<1e-6, or |f|>1e9, reinterpret the 4 bytes as int32. Distribution of raw off4 values across 1137 SPEL EFITs: 0(334), 100(226), 10(214), 20(169), 5(136), 50(119), 30(87), 15(84), 25(82), 1(41).

MGEF actorValue (DATA off8) semantics for all 145 MGEFs: 0 = special/generic (LOCK, OPEN, DISPL, TELE, VAMP, ...); 8 = Health (ABHE, DGHE, ...); 9 = Magicka ('SP'=spell points; Restore Magicka=RESP); 10 = Fatigue; 11 = Speed (BRDN, FTHR); 33-70 = skills/attributes (CALM=33, CHML=46, INVI=47, PARA=48, SLNC=49, RSPA=66, ...); >100 = FormID link - ALL 62 Conjuration MGEFs are FormID links (Bound Weapons BW01-08, Summons Z001-19, Bound Armor BABO-BASH). Use threshold 200 to split actorValue from linkedFormID.

Oblivion SPEL records do NOT store a magic school; it must be derived from the spell's magic effects. Because EFID holds an editorID code rather than a formID, references cannot be resolved during the single decode pass. Implemented a two-phase scheme: ESMFile::resolveMagicReferences() runs after all records are decoded and maps effectCodes -> effectFormIDs and derives spell.school from the first effect's MGEF school. ESMManager::rebuildIndices() runs a SECOND pass that builds a global editorID->MGEF map across all loaded files and re-resolves each file, so DLC plugin spells link to master (Oblivion.esm) MGEFs. MagicEffectData pointers in ESMManager::m_magicEffectByEditorID are only valid after rebuildIndices() (it clears them on every rebuild).

game/spell_manager.cpp mgefToEffectType() now takes const oblivion::MagicEffectData* instead of a formID. The old hardcoded formID switch (0x0001E825 etc.) was entirely wrong: real MGEF formIDs are 0x00001881-style, so every effect fell back to DAMAGE. Classification now keys off the MGEF editorID code plus school/linkedFormID: FIDG/FRDG/SHDG/DG*/DR*/WK*/AB* -> DAMAGE, REHE/FOHE/CU* -> HEAL, RESP/FOSP/FOMM -> RESTORE_MANA, REFA/FOFA -> RESTORE_STAMINA, PARA -> PARALYZE, INVI -> INVISIBILITY, school==1 && linkedFormID!=0 -> SUMMON, fallback = DAMAGE when school==2 else FORTIFY_ATTR.

ESM subrecord layouts (confirmed): PGRD: PGRP 16B stride (xyz float + unused u32), PGAG 1 bit/point, PGRR 4B stride, PGRL 12 raw B; no own cell FormID (use GRUP parent); always compressed (flag bit18), decompress before decode. GMST: EDID + DATA typed by first EDID char (s/f/i/b). GLOB: EDID+FNAM(1,type)+FLTV(4). LTEX: EDID+ICON+HNAM(3 rgb)+SNAM(1). DOOR: EDID+FULL+MODL+MODB(4)+SCRI(4)+SNAM(4)+ANAM(4)+FNAM(1). GRAS: EDID+MODL+MODB(4)+DATA(32; off2 maxSlope). FURN: EDID+FULL+MODL+MODB(4)+MNAM(4). AMMO: EDID+FULL+MODL+MODB(4)+ICON+ENAM(4)+DATA(18). SLGM: EDID+FULL+MODL+MODB(4)+ICON+SCRI(4)+DATA(8)+SOUL(1)+SLCP(1). KEYM: EDID+FULL+MODL+MODB(4)+ICON+DATA(8). SBSP: EDID+DNAM(12, 3 floats). SGST: EDID+FULL+MODL+MODB(4)+MODT(96)+ICON+repeated EFID(4)+EFIT(24)+DATA(9). WTHR: EDID+CNAM+DNAM+NAM0(160)+FNAM(16)+HNAM(56)+DATA(15)+SNAM(8)*N. IDLE: EDID+MODL+MODB(4)+CTDA(24)*N+ANAM(1)+DATA(8). CSTY: EDID+CSTD(124; first 2 B u16 weaponFlags + floats). LSCR: EDID+ICON+DESC+LNAM(12; first 4=FormID). ANIO: EDID+MODL+MODB(4)+DATA(4, FormID). WATR: EDID+TNAM+ANAM(1)+FNAM(1)+MNAM(1)+SNAM(4)+DATA(102 floats)+GNAM(12). EFSH: EDID+ICON(1)+ICO2+DATA(224; first int32s are flag groups).

ESM pitfall: LAND, PGRD, REFR, ACHR and ACRE records do not carry their own cell formID. The owning cell must be recovered by tracking the label of the enclosing GRUP with groupType == 6 (CellChildren). Two code paths need this: the file parse path uses a groupInfoStack and the memory parse path uses m_currentCellFormID. Oblivion GRUP types: 0=TopLevel, 1=WorldChildren, 2=InteriorCellBlock, 3=InteriorCellSubBlock, 4=ExteriorCellBlock, 5=ExteriorCellSubBlock, 6=CellChildren, 7=TopicChildren, 8=CellPersistentChildren, 9=CellTemporaryChildren. Also note SubRecord has no empty() member; use size() > 0.

The reference title screen has NO selection highlight: the six menu labels have almost identical ink density (76.2/69.6/70.3/71.9/74.1/72.3). The port still needs an input affordance, so the selected item is shown by interpolating COLOR_MENU_TEXT -> COLOR_MENU_TEXT_SELECTED plus a thin underline under the baseline.

The reference menu row is BASELINE aligned, not top aligned: every glyph's ink bottom sits on the same row (y=287/360 = 0.7972H) while the ink top varies per glyph (C=8, o=11, p=15 row offsets). So the layout must place glyphs by baseline. TextRenderer exposes getTextCapHeight() for this.

Oblivion .fnt files carry NO vertical metrics (header bytes 76..344 are all zero), and f[1] is NOT an advance. Glyph boxes are tight ink bboxes plus ~1px padding, so advance = width and bearing_x = 0. Vertical metrics are measured at runtime from the atlas: capBaseline = mode of the ink-bottom row of ASCII 'A'-'Z', and per glyph baseline_rel = min(inkBottom, capBaseline). For kingthings_regular (fontSize 28, 512x512 atlas) capBaseline = 24. Glyph records are indexed by ASCII - 1.

text_renderer.cpp: when scanning a glyph box for its ink bottom you must walk EVERY row and keep the last row that has ink. Writing the loop as 'for (y = 0; y < h && last < 0; y++)' stops at the FIRST inked row and records the ink TOP, which made capBaseline collapse to 1 and pushed the whole menu row ~63px too high.

TitleScreen must apply its plain font style ONCE (applyPlainFontStyle in render(), guarded by fontStyleApplied) and restore it when leaving the title (releasePlainFontStyle on gameStarted/quitRequested). Saving/restoring setFontAlphaCurveEnabled/setFontOutlineEnabled/setFontSizeMultiplier every frame emitted 6 INFO lines per frame and made computeMenuLayout see a different fontSizeMultiplier_ than the draw call.

TextRenderer::getTextWidth()/getTextCapHeight() fold fontSizeMultiplier_ into their result, so a layout computed at one moment and drawn at another disagree. TitleScreen::computeMenuLayout() and rebuildMenuLayout() therefore divide the measured width/cap height by the current getFontSizeMultiplier() to normalise to multiplier 1.0, which is what the title screen draws with.

Correction: the ink alpha curve is NOT a meaningful legibility lever. Outline width is CLAMPED, so most values are no-ops at title scale: drawOblivionText() uses ring = clamp(fontScale * fontOutlineWidth_, 0.6f, 3.0f). Phase 66 P19 device verification found the real root cause of slow-motion gameplay: jni_bridge.cpp nativeRenderFrame passed the constant 0.0167f (60 fps) to Renderer::render(), so the simulation advanced one 60 Hz frame per RENDERED frame. Measured on the emulator (16-19 fps): gamestate reported time=12:00 and 60 real seconds later time=12:09, where timescale 30 demands 12:30 - about 32% of real time. Because the same deltaTime is forwarded to ImperialWeave, every dt-driven phase was affected (animation, AI, physics, combat, video decode, sun orbit). FIX: measure the interval with std::chrono::steady_clock, clamp to kMaxDelta = 0.1f (about a 10 fps floor) so a long cell load or a background return cannot teleport the world, fall back to 1/60 s on the first frame, and clear the marker in nativeCleanup and in the nativeInitEngine resume path.

The fixed-dt bug could not be caught by run_host_tests.sh: jni_bridge.cpp depends on Android-only headers and is not in the harness SOURCES. Any logic that lives only in the JNI layer is invisible to CI. Follow-up improvement I1: extract the frame pacing into an Android-independent FrameClock class under engine/ so the measured-dt, clamp and reset behaviour can be host-tested.

XTEL holds the DESTINATION DOOR REFR FormID, not a cell, so the destination cell is resolved one hop later: Renderer::registerEsmDoors() indexes refs and cells, maps door REFR -> target REFR -> target cellFormID, and bakes the result into Door.destinationCell / destinationIsWorldspace. DoorManager stays ESM-agnostic. Registration must run inside createTestScenario after the reference loop, not at world build time, because initializeTestCells only creates test cells and interior cells are skipped by addCellFromESM.

Door transition ordering (door.cpp performCellTransition): (1) write player position/rotation BEFORE switching cells, because leaveInteriorCell() resolves the return exterior cell from the recorded position; (2) interior -> enterInteriorCell(formID, editorID, fullName), exterior -> getCellByFormID() then leaveInteriorCell() only if wasIndoors, then loadCell(cellX, cellY); (3) skip updateActiveCells() while indoors - interior positions are cell relative and streaming would pull back the exterior cell at the same coordinate. The usedoor command filters candidates with getDoorsInCell(currentCell->tesFormID) before the distance compare for the same reason.
